title: FORGETTING THE ROCK WHO BORE US

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You deserted the Rock, who fathered you; you forgot the God who gave you birth." — Deut 32:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This single verse captures the heartbreak at the centre of the whole song: "You deserted the Rock, who fathered you; you forgot the God who gave you birth." The tragedy of sin is here distilled into two painful words — deserted and forgot. The people turned away from the very God who had given them life, who had fathered them, who had brought them into being. There is deep sorrow in these words, the sorrow of a parent whose child has forgotten them.

Forgetting is at the root of so much of our spiritual drifting. We do not usually decide, in one dramatic moment, to abandon God. Rather, we simply forget — forget His goodness, forget His faithfulness, forget how He has carried us. And as the memory fades, so does our devotion. What we forget, we begin to desert.

This is why Scripture constantly calls us to remember. Remembering God's faithfulness is not just a nice sentiment; it is a lifeline that keeps us from drifting. When we actively recall who God is and all He has done, our hearts are drawn back to Him in love and gratitude.

The wonder of the gospel is that even when we forget God, He does not forget us. He remembers His covenant, He pursues His wandering children, and in Christ He has done everything to bring us back. Jesus gave us the bread and cup precisely so we would "do this in remembrance" of Him (Luke 22:19). So fight forgetfulness. Remember the Rock who fathered you, the God who gave you life — and let remembering keep you close to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. In what ways have I "forgotten" God's goodness and faithfulness?
2. How does actively remembering God keep me from drifting?
3. What is one truth about God I need to remember afresh today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for the times I have forgotten You, the Rock who gave me life. Help me remember Your faithfulness and never desert You. Thank You that even when I forget, You never forget me. Amen.
